/reports/afrique-de-louest-et-du-centre-.title: Afrique de l'Ouest et du Centre — Dosso (Niger) et Kebbi (Nigéria) — Cartographie des transhumance bloqués 1 (Avril 2022)
/reports/afrique-de-louest-et-du-centre-.summary: La transhumance transfrontalière est une pratique d'élevage majeure en Afrique de l'Ouest et du Centre, et en particulier dans la région du Sahel. Activité économique importante et moteur de développement régional, la transhumance a, au cours des dernières décennies, fait l'objet d'importantes mutations. Les variations climatiques, la pression démographique, la concurrence croissante pour des ressources plus rares, la volatilité politique et l'insécurité ont profondément affecté les itinéraires, les calendriers et les flux de transhumance.​

/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%93-gssss-monguno.title: Nigeria – GSSSS Monguno Fire Outbreak Flash Report (24 May 2020)
/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%93-gssss-monguno.summary: On 22nd May 2020, a fire broke out at the Government Senior Science Secondary School (GSSSS) Camp, Monguno. The resultant damage left 124 individuals (31 households) without shelters and properties. It was reported that 35 makeshift shelters and one transitional shelter (constructed by the International Committee of the Red Cross or ICRC) was burnt.

/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-covid-19-situ.summary: COVID-19 Situation Analysis is based on assessment of knowledge, impact and practice of internally displaced persons (IDPs) and impacted populations in the six conflict-affected states of northeastern Nigeria. /reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-dalori-ii-fla.title: Nigeria — Dalori II Flash Report (13 April 2017)
/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-dalori-ii-fla.summary: On 12 April 2017 at about 9:10 pm, suspected Boko Haram insurgents attacked the military station situated behind Dalori II (250 Housing Estate Camp), less than 2 kilometers from the camp. Majority of the IDPs headed towards Maiduguri while some others tried going to Dalori I but they were denied access by the security at the gate. /reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-displacement-.title: Nigeria — Displacement Dashboard 13 (1 July 2014—31 December 2016)
/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-displacement-.summary: As of the 31 December, the conflict in the northeastern part of Nigeria has left an estimated 1,770,444 people displaced across 6 most affected states. The largest IDP populations are located in Adamawa (440 sites), followed by Borno (424 sites), Yobe (401 sites), Bauchi (322), Taraba (213) and Gombe (148). 92% of the IDP locations are classified as host communities. 88% of the IDP population have been displaced within their original state. Report includes sectoral analysis summary.

The largest IDP populations were in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe. 97.2% of the IDPs were displaced because of the Boko Haram conflict.

/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-displacements.summary: An assessment was carried out on 17 August 2017 by the DTM team in response to the displacement of persons into Madagali LGA. The assessment team conﬁrmed that 3 villages (Bakin-Dutse, humbili and Wuno) were recently affected by Boko Haram attacks. Two of the villages, Bakin-Dutse and Humbili were attacked on 8 and 9 August respectively, while the people of Wuno ﬂed, fearing a possible attack on their village.  A total of 216 households and 1,511 individuals were displaced from the villages. The displaced persons are currently staying at Lomure Gulak and gare Gulak.

/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-flood-adamawa.title: Nigeria — Flood in Adamawa State Flash Report (29 October 2019)
/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-flood-adamawa.summary: Following heavy rains on 26-27 October 2019, a large number of people have been displaced in Lamurde, Numan, Demsa, Guyuk, Girei, Fufore, Yola North and Yola South Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Nigeria’s northeastern state of Adamawa. An estimated 381 houses have been damaged, 493 houses partially damaged, with over 365 water and sanitation facilities destroyed, affecting 12,092 individuals (2,325 households). In Purakayo ward of Guyuk LGA, 2 people were reportedly killed by the flash floods and an unconfirmed number of people injured in the eight affected LGAs of Adamawa.

/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-flood-geidam-.title: Nigeria — Flood in Geidam Flash Report  (19 August 2019)
/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-flood-geidam-.summary: Incessant rains have led to the displacement of some residents of Asheikri, Kawuri, Hausari, Ma’anna/Dagambi, Balle/Gallaba/Melari and Gumsa wards in the Geidam Local Government Area (LGA) of the northeastern state of Yobe. An estimated 318 houses have been damaged, affecting 2,802 individuals (431 households). Asheikri, Kawuri and Hausari were the most affected wards, hosting a combined 1,716 individuals (61%) of the displaced individuals.

/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-flow-monitori.title: Nigeria — Flow Monitoring Dashboard 10 (1—31 December 2017)
/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-flow-monitori.summary: This dashboard provides an overview of mobility patterns occurring in Nigeria’s northern States of Kano and Sokoto in December 2017. Results show that the daily average number of individuals observed at the flow monitoring point (FMP) in Sokoto decreased by 1% compared to November. Some changes were observed in the age distribution of migrants, with more minor travelers observed in December, representing a 5 percentage point increase from the previous month. The number of female migrants observed at the FMP decreased 20%, while male migrants decreased 62%.

/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-flow-monitori.title: Nigeria — Flow Monitoring Dashboard 11 (1—31 January 2018)

Results for Sokoto show that the daily average number of individuals observed at the flow monitoring points increased by 3% compared to December. Some changes were observed in the age distribution of migrants, with an increase in adult male and female travelers observed in January, representing a 7 percentage point increase from the previous month. For 54% of individuals, Nigeria is the country of departure, while the remaining 46% are leaving from Niger.

/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-location-base.title: Nigeria — Location Based Assessment Report 13 (1 July 2014—31 December 2016)
/reports/nigeria-%E2%80%94-location-base.summary: As of 31 December, the conflict in the northeastern part of Nigeria has left an estimated 1,770,444 people displaced across the 6 most affected states. The largest IDP populations are located in Adamawa (440 sites), followed by Borno (424 sites), Yobe (401 sites), Bauchi (322), Taraba (213) and Gombe (148). 92% of the IDP locations are classified as host communities. 88% of the IDP population have been displaced within their original state. The report includes a sectoral analysis summary.

Following the reopening of the road, about 3,000 IDPs of Bama origin at Dalori I and II Camps in Maiduguri were relocated to Bama town by the Government of Nigeria (GoN), on 2 April 2018. /reports/nigeria-borno-state-idp-intenti.title: Nigeria — Borno State - IDP Intention Survey (June 2025)
/reports/nigeria-borno-state-idp-intenti.summary: The IDP Intention Survey conducted in Borno State provides critical insights into the future intentions of internally displaced persons (IDPs) residing in camps and camp-like settings. The survey, implemented by the Borno State Government in collaboration with key partners including Ministry of Reconstruction, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (MRRR), Borno State Emergency Management Agency (BOSEMA), Borno State Ministry of Budget And Planning, Borno State Ministry of Information & Internal Security, Ministry of Women Affairs, Borno State Agency for Coordination of Sustainable Development and Hu

/reports/nigeria-borno-state-intention-s.title: Nigeria — Borno State - Intention Survey - El Miskin Camp I (August 2024)
/reports/nigeria-borno-state-intention-s.summary: El Miskin Camp I, containing 1,754 households (totaling 11,110 individuals), reported that 48 per cent of its residents had been displaced multiple times, while 52 per cent experienced displacement only once. Among those displaced multiple times, 40 per cent were displaced twice. In 2016, El Miskin Camp I recorded the highest number of new arrivals (58%), primarily displaced due to insurgency.

/reports/nigeria-borno-state-intention-s.title: Nigeria — Borno State - Intention Survey - El Miskin Camp II (August 2024)
/reports/nigeria-borno-state-intention-s.summary: El Miskin Camp II, which provides shelter to 3,182 households (totaling 19,891 individuals), reported that 53 per cent of residents experienced displacement only once, 47 per cent had faced multiple displacements, with 38 per cent of those individuals displaced twice. The camp’s largest influx of new arrivals occurred in 2016, with 56 per cent of its residents displaced as a result of insurgency.

/reports/nigeria-borno-state-intention-s.title: Nigeria — Borno State - Intention Survey - Madinatu Camp (August 2024)
/reports/nigeria-borno-state-intention-s.summary: Madinatu Camp, which shelters 3,833 households and a total of 26,454 individuals, reported that 55 per cent of residents had experienced displacement only once, while 45 per cent had faced multiple displacements. Of those displaced multiple times, 36 per cent were displaced twice. In 2016, the camp saw its largest influx of new arrivals, with 45 per cent arriving primarily due to insurgency.

/reports/nigeria-borno-state-intention-s.title: Nigeria — Borno State - Intention Survey - Muna El Badawy Camp (August 2024)
/reports/nigeria-borno-state-intention-s.summary: Muna El Badawy Camp, housing 6,289 households (totaling 39,658 individuals), reported that 43 per cent of its households had been displaced multiple times, while 57 per cent experienced displacement only once. Among those displaced multiple times, 34 per cent were displaced twice. In 2016, Muna El Badawy Camp recorded the highest number of new arrivals (49%), primarily displaced due to insurgency.

/reports/nigeria-kaduna-state-intention-.title: Nigeria — Kaduna State - Intention Survey (August 2024)

Four individuals sustained injuries during the incident; no fatalities were reported.

The incidents also resulted in four fatalities.

/reports/nigeria-yobe-state-idp-intentio.title: Nigeria — Yobe State - IDP Intention Survey (August 2025)
/reports/nigeria-yobe-state-idp-intentio.summary: The IDP Intention Survey conducted in Yobe State provides critical insights into the future intentions of internally displaced persons (IDPs) residing in camps and camp-like settings. The survey, implemented by the Yobe State Government in collaboration with key partners, including Yobe State Emergency Management Agency (YOSEMA), National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs, Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Agency (RUWASA), Ministry of Agriculture, Ministry of Basic Education, Ministry of Budget, Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Health & Human Services

/reports/nigeria-zamfara-intention-surve.title: Nigeria — Zamfara - Intention Survey (August 2024)
/reports/nigeria-zamfara-intention-surve.summary: To ascertain the future intentions and aspirations of the IDPs in Zamfara State, the DTM surveyed 13 LGAs where IDPs were situated. Out of the 23,668 displaced households in the state, 2,366 were interviewed. Among the households interviewed, 10 per cent resided in camps and camp-like settings while the remaining 90 per cent were situated in host communities.

/reports/west-and-central-africa-dosso-n.title: West and Central Africa — Dosso (Niger) and Kebbi (Nigeria) — Mapping of Stranded Herders 1 (April 2022)
/reports/west-and-central-africa-dosso-n.summary: Cross-border transhumance is a major herding practice in West and Central Africa, and especially in the Sahel region. As an important economic activity and a driver of regional development, transhumance has, in the past few decades, been subject to significant changes. Climatic variation, demographic pressure, growing competition over scarcer resources, political volatility and insecurity have deeply affected transhumant routes, patterns and flows.

/reports/west-and-central-africa-nigeria.title: West and Central Africa — Nigeria North-West and North-Central Crisis Monthly Dashboard 1 (23 December 2022)

/reports/west-and-central-africa-stabili.title: West and Central Africa — Stability Index — Cameroon and Nigeria (September 2019)
/reports/west-and-central-africa-stabili.summary: A report by IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) identified 4.2 million displaced individuals in Nigeria, Chad, and Cameroon in 2019. However, as the protracted conflict begins to subside in some regions, there are a growing number of displaced persons returning to their towns and villages of origin. The DTM noted a 77 per cent increase (800,000 individuals) in the number of returnees in 2019 compare those reported in 2016.
